speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Recent events in the US have highlighted the risks of excessive trading driving sharp movements in price.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: There are important lessons to learn from this experience, and we need to be alert to similar risks potentially occurring in our own markets.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: While investigations by the US authorities are on-going, the triggers for the recent event were not unfamiliar to the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Certain investors had accumulated large short positions, exerting downward price pressure in the affected stocks.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This was followed by online discussions amongst retail investors to buy the stocks, which increased their prices.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: There are, by and large, two scenarios we are safeguarding against.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: One is the “pump and dump” scenario, where certain parties incite trading to push up prices, including through online forums and social media chat groups.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Once prices rise to specific levels, they may sell then the securities which they had accumulated earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: When prices eventually fall back down, other investors could suffer quite heavy losses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A second scenario is the “short and distort” scenario, where certain investors take a short position on certain securities and use false or misleading information to encourage more short-selling.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They can make profits by covering their positions after prices have fallen.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our safeguards address such scenarios in three ways.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: When there are unusual price movements in a company’s securities, SGX RegCo may issue a query and the company must publicly clarify if it is undertaking any activity that would warrant such a price change.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If market rumours are influencing stock prices, the company is required to provide a prompt and full response to any allegations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As an early warning to investors, SGX RegCo may also issue a “Trade with Caution” alert on securities where there is potential for disorderly trading.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In addition, aggregated short positions and trading volumes are published for each security.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These measures provide transparency to investors, allowing the market to self-correct where there is excessive trading that is not backed by business fundamentals.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Second, to curb the effect of a sharp movement in the price of a security, a circuit breaker may be triggered that temporarily suspends trading.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX may also impose additional conditions such as restricting specific market participants from trading or requiring investors to place more collateral.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In extreme cases, affected securities may be suspended from trading altogether until further notice.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In particular, it is illegal under the Securities and Futures Act to disseminate misleading information or use manipulative and deceptive practices.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS and SGX RegCo have recently issued statements advising investors on the risks of trading in securities based on discussions on online forums.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Investors should refer to these advisories and be alert to the risks of trading in a volatile market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first is, with our safeguards in place, what is the likelihood of short squeezes happening in Singapore and thus, leading to massive market dislocations?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second question that I have is, what is MAS' position on having platforms like Robinhood being set up in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We know that Robinhood was one of the key platforms that Reddit band had used to try to corner the market, create short squeezes and thus, create massive market dislocations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would we put in safeguards to prevent them from setting up in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Or would we create a regulatory environment that will control their behaviour, like what we have seen in the US?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As to the reasons why, there can be a few hypotheses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One, maybe, it is the culture of investors here.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Two, it is also the level of disclosure; so, if you are a listed company, there is a high level or standard that you have to abide to in disclosing your business and if anything that is happening that is material to your business.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for platforms, you know how online platforms are.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think, ultimately, it is still about having a good, transparent, efficient regulatory regime and functioning of the market to prevent such things from happening in the first place.
